summary: Tested the admin custom watermark logo upload and reset (backend, stream burn-in and UI). All requested items pass. Backend (new file test_watermark_upload.py, 10 tests, all pass): no token returns 401/403; a non-admin gets 403 on POST and on DELETE; text/plain returns 400; a corrupt file sent as image/png returns 400; a file over 5MB returns 413; JPEG and WEBP are accepted and converted to PNG; a 600x400 PNG is resized to 360x240; settings.watermark_path and watermark_version are set; GET /api/watermark returns the custom PNG. Stream burn-in: a free user's 720p stream, recorded through the local RTMP listener, shows the red custom logo top-left (red ratio 1.0 in the logo box). After rm /tmp/creatorlive_branding/*, the next stream downloads the logo again from storage and still burns it. DELETE returns the default logo, byte-identical to assets/watermark.png, and the stream then has no custom logo. Full regression: 75/78 passed on the first run. The 3 failures were 2 stale assertions in test_admin.py and 1 flaky test in test_watermark.py, which I fixed in the test harness and re-ran (16/16 watermark tests pass). UI with admin+clerk_test: the preview shows the default logo (626x98) and the 'Use default' button is hidden. After upload, the success toast appears, the preview src ?v= changes to the new version (600x200 custom image) and 'Use default' appears. A .txt upload shows the error toast 'Upload a PNG, JPG or WEBP image'. The switch goes checked, then unchecked, then checked. 'Use default' shows the toast 'Default CreatorLive24/7 logo restored', the preview returns to the default and the button is hidden. Step 3 studio as a free creator: studio-watermark src=/api/watermark?v=<current version> shows the custom logo (600x200). Final state: default logo (watermark_path null) and watermark_enabled true.

minor.issue: Old custom logo objects are never deleted from storage, and old /tmp/creatorlive_branding/*.png files are never cleaned up (orphan files after each re-upload). Low impact.
The type check uses the client-sent content_type only. The PIL decode then catches non-images, so this is safe, but a real PNG sent with type application/octet-stream is rejected.

issues: studio-watermark-note still says 'the CreatorLive24/7 logo appears' even when the admin uploaded a custom logo. Consider wording like 'our logo'.

action_items: Optional: update test_admin.py TestPublic.test_seeded_plans and TestPayments.test_flow. They assume seeded plan values (Starter 30 days, Pro 499 with no offer), but the real admin has edited the plans (Starter is 45 days, Pro has an active offer of 299). These are stale test assertions, not app bugs.
Optional: generalise the studio free-plan note text for custom logos; delete the old storage object when the logo is replaced or reset.
critical_code_review_comments: watermark_file(): if the storage download fails it silently falls back to the default logo. That is reasonable, but nothing is logged, so add a logger.warning.
/api/watermark sends Cache-Control max-age=300. The frontend busts the cache with ?v=watermark_version, so this is OK. ffmpeg uses the local file, so it is not affected.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_watermark.py (record_stream listener -t 6 -> 12; the listener used to close before the 3s status check, so the stream got a Broken pipe; this was a test flake)

success_rate.backend: 100% of watermark tests (16/16); full suite 75/78 with 3 test-side issues (2 stale plan assertions, 1 timing flake, now fixed)

seed_data_creation: none (TEST_wm videos are created and deleted by the fixtures)
flaky_tests: test_watermark.py record_stream: with listener -t 6 there was about a 30-50% Broken pipe failure (the stream ends before the status check). Fixed with -t 12.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the watermark tests with: cd /app/backend/tests && python -m pytest test_watermark.py test_watermark_upload.py -n0 (pytest.ini adds -n). Do NOT create files under /app/backend while streams are running: WatchFiles reloads the backend and kills ffmpeg. Single-use UI tickets: python /tmp/tickets.py prints ADMIN and CREATOR tickets; you can rebuild it from conftest bapi /sign_in_tokens. The creator's YouTube destination is set to the local RTMP rtmp://127.0.0.1:1935/live2 by the tests, and the studio shows a 'Last stream stopped: Broken pipe' banner left over from the test streams.
